claims.text: The arrival that starts the free wait is not established on this record. Under the category's arrival test the driver is at the pickup only when the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m and the 120 s window, and the trace's own derived arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null. The 13:11:50 'driver arrived' event therefore rests on the driver's button press alone, and the driver's counterparty statement ('I was there') has nothing behind it but that button. EV-GPS-06061 is impaired - issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight_multiplier 0.6 - its only gap being 640 s, from 13:08:50 to 13:19:30, which straddles the arrival marker, the free-wait window and the cancellation, with the fixes either side several hundred metres from the pickup.

The trace is silent on the one interval the fee depends on. The free wait for this on-demand trip runs 13:11:50 to 13:16:50 under POL-NS-21, and EV-GPS-06061 carries no fix inside it at all: the single 640 s gap swallows the entire waiting window, coverage_pct is 28.6 and there are 8 fixes against a 30 s expected interval. That artifact is impaired - GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight 0.6 - so the interval the driver's presence turns on is precisely the interval with no location evidence, and POL-GEN-02 caps any confidence in it at 0.6.

POL-NS-22 charges the 5.00 SGD fee only where the driver cancels after the free wait, and for an on-demand trip POL-NS-21 starts that wait at the driver's arrival. The record's 390 s is measured from an arrival event that the GPS trace does not corroborate, so the fee's precondition is not made out on this evidence: a 5.00 SGD charge cannot stand on a timer whose start has no support beyond the app's own button press.

The fact this case turns on - whether the driver was at Block 14, and when - cannot be established, because the only artifact that could corroborate it is impaired across exactly the relevant interval. POL-GEN-26 provides that where a fact a rule of this version needs cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired, the case is escalated and the open question stated, and no outcome is inferred from the absence except where a rule says so. EV-GPS-06061 is impaired (GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight 0.6). ESCALATE is the rider-favourable reading here: the 5.00 SGD is held rather than collected, while NO_ACTION would leave the rider carrying it.

POL-NS-24 refunds in full any fee charged where the driver fails to arrive at the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes. This trip was on-demand with no scheduled_at, so the deadline cannot be fixed from the record (driver_deadline.deadline is null) - and the arrival that would fix it is uncorroborated. On the clause's own reading, where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies. Either way the charge is not left standing on this record: the driver either did not arrive (full refund) or arrival cannot be established (escalation, fee held). EV-GPS-06061 is impaired, issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight 0.6.

The money is still with the platform and still on the rider. EV-FARE-06061 shows payment_status CHARGED, cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the rider is out of pocket the whole contested amount. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is read party-relative against the rider who filed: the rider is owed the disputed charge back, so any ruling that voids the fee is FULL_REFUND of the whole 5.00 SGD (the ledger's refund_if_voided_sgd is 5.00), and NO_ACTION would simply preserve the present state in which the rider pays.

The rider does not put its case on POL-NS-23, and says so plainly rather than stretching the point: EV-CHAT-06061 shows two in-app messages (13:12:10 and 13:15:00) and EV-TRIP-06061 shows one in-app call placed at 13:14:20, all before the 13:18:20 cancellation, and the derived obligation_met is true. The contact limb is met on the face of the record. The rider's case is the arrival limb, not this one.

claims.text: This is an on-demand trip — scheduled_at is null — so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival, not from any schedule. The trip record shows the driver marking arrived at 13:11:50, the free-wait timer starting at 13:11:55 and expiring at 13:16:55, and the cancellation at 13:18:20: 390 s after arrival, 90 s past the end of the free wait. On those timings the driver cancelled only after the wait had fully run, which is exactly what POL-NS-21 permits.

POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the driver failed to message AND call before cancelling. Both limbs are satisfied on the COMPLETE records: the chat log carries two in-app messages sent by the driver, at 13:12:10 and 13:15:00, and the trip record carries an in-app call placed by the driver at 13:14:20 — all three before the 13:18:20 cancellation. The clause requires a call to be placed, not answered, so the 20 s unanswered ring-out satisfies it. The contact obligation is met and there is no ground to void the fee.

The payments ledger shows exactly 5.00 SGD charged for the cancellation — the policy fee — with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has yet moved. Under POL-NS-22, where the free wait has run and the fee stands, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged, 5.00 SGD; POL-GEN-03 confirms that figure is the money the ruling moves, not a second payment.

No FULL_REFUND is available to the rider on this record. On a no-show charge only POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-24 favour the rider, and both fail: the contact obligation was met (POL-NS-23), and POL-NS-24 needs a scheduled pickup time the driver missed by five minutes, but this trip is on-demand with scheduled_at null, so there is no scheduled time to miss and no deadline to fix. The rider's 'he never came' account therefore has no refund clause to stand on, and the present charge must be left intact.

I disclose rather than hide the state of the trace: the GPS artifact is IMPAIRED, weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, and its derived arrival check reports corroborated false with nearest_fix null. It cannot be presented as clean corroboration. But a 640 s gap is absent data, not evidence that the driver was somewhere else, and the arrival event, the 'driver has arrived' push notification to the rider at 13:11:54 and the free-wait timer are all carried independently on the COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0. The impairment caps the weight of the trace; it does not erase the platform record of arrival.

Even on the most sceptical reading of the impaired trace — that the arrival is not GPS-corroborated — the result is not a refund. POL-GEN-26 sends a case to human review precisely where a needed fact (here, when the driver arrived) cannot be established on impaired evidence, and on escalation the amount is held, not returned. That is the floor of this case, and it still leaves the 5.00 SGD with the driver rather than the rider.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee on TRP-06061 is neither collected nor refunded. It is held, and the case goes to a human reviewer.

Why the case cannot be decided on this record. The fee stands only if the driver cancelled after the 5-minute free wait. This was an on-demand trip — EV-TRIP-06061 shows scheduled_at null — so under POL-NS-21 the free wait runs from the driver's arrival, and the arrival is decided by the category's arrival test: the trip record's arrival event must be corroborated by the GPS trace inside the STANDARD 50 m radius and the 120 s window. The only artifact that could supply that corroboration, EV-GPS-06061, is impaired — issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight_multiplier 0.6 — with one 640 s gap from 13:08:50 to 13:19:30 that swallows the 13:11:50 arrival marker, the whole free-wait window (13:11:50–13:16:50) and the 13:18:20 cancellation, and its own arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null. The arrival is therefore undecided, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation where a fact a rule needs — here, when the driver arrived — cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is impaired. Confidence is 0.6, capped under POL-GEN-02(2) by that record, the only artifact that could carry the deciding fact; no independent artifact carries it, so nothing lifts the cap.

The driver's case. The timings on EV-TRIP-06061 (arrival 13:11:50, cancellation 13:18:20, 390 s after arrival, 90 s past the free wait) are correct as recorded, but they run from an arrival the arrival test does not corroborate; an arrival tap records only that the driver pressed the button, and POL-NS-21's test needs the GPS corroboration the impaired trace cannot give. So the argument that the COMPLETE trip record (weight 1.0) independently establishes the arrival, and the claim for DRIVER_COMPENSATION under POL-NS-22, are rejected: the fee's precondition is undecided, not made out. The counterparty statement ('I was there, messaged and called') and the chat messages ('Reached Blk 14 drop off', 13:12:10; 'Waiting', 13:15:00) are accounts offered over a stretch where the test admitted no reading; they do not stand in for the test.

What is accepted for the driver: the POL-NS-23 contact obligation is met — EV-CHAT-06061 carries two in-app messages (13:12:10, 13:15:00) and EV-TRIP-06061 one in-app call (13:14:20, unanswered, 20 s), all before the 13:18:20 cancellation — so the fee is not voided on that ground, and the rider concedes this.

The rider's case. Your POL-NS-24 route to a refund fails on its own terms: the clause needs a scheduled pickup time the driver missed by five minutes, and this trip is on-demand with no scheduled time; the clause's own note sends an unfixable deadline to POL-GEN-26, which is escalation — so neither FULL_REFUND nor a standing charge follows. Your account that you were downstairs the whole time is noted, but the location evidence cannot resolve the conflict, and the money state you cite (EV-FARE-06061: cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is accepted only as the sum now held.

Money. EV-FARE-06061 shows 5.00 SGD charged and 0.00 refunded; that contested 5.00 is held, not collected or refunded, and both amount fields are null on escalation.

Referrals: none. The fee equals the policy fee of 5.00 SGD, so no POL-NS-22 referral fires; contact was attempted, so no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit; and the rider profile carries no repeat no-show counter, so no POL-NS-25 flag.

Open question for the reviewer: was the driver physically at Block 14 at 13:11:50? It should be resolved from location evidence (for example vehicle telematics) alongside the parties' accounts.

ruling.explanation:
The 5.00 SGD no-show fee on trip TRP-06061 cannot be decided on this record, so the case goes to a human reviewer and the 5.00 SGD is held rather than collected or refunded.

Why it cannot be decided. Under POL-NS-21 the free wait for this on-demand trip (scheduled_at is null) runs from the driver's arrival, and the fee under POL-NS-22 stands only if the driver cancelled after that wait. The arrival at 13:11:50 is carried only by the driver's arrival tap on the trip record, and the category's arrival test requires that event to be corroborated by the GPS trace within the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m and the 120 s window. EV-GPS-06061 is IMPAIRED, weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION: one 640 s gap (13:08:50 to 13:19:30) swallows the arrival marker, the whole 13:11:50-13:16:50 waiting window and the 13:18:20 cancellation, coverage is 28.6%, and the artifact's own arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null; the fixes either side are several hundred metres from Block 14, Eunos Crescent. The limb that would establish the driver was at the pickup is therefore undecided over exactly the stretch the defect covers, and it supports neither upholding the fee nor voiding it. POL-GEN-26 speaks to precisely this: where when the driver arrived cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is impaired, the case is escalated and the open question stated.

The driver's claims. The POL-NS-21 timing claim is factually right about the trip record's clock (arrival 13:11:50, wait expired 13:16:55, cancellation 13:18:20, 390 s from arrival, 90 s past the 300 s free wait), but the clock's start is the disputed fact, and the driver's further claim that the COMPLETE arrival event, the 13:11:54 push notification and the wait timer carry the arrival independently is rejected: all three are produced by the same arrival tap, and POL-NS-21's own test reads the arrival event plus GPS corroboration, not the tap alone. The POL-NS-23 contact claim is accepted: the COMPLETE chat log carries two driver messages (13:12:10, 13:15:00) and the trip record a driver in-app call (13:14:20, unanswered 20 s), all before 13:18:20, and the rider concedes the limb. The POL-NS-22 / POL-GEN-03 claim that the fee stands and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD is rejected, because the fee's precondition is the very limb left undecided. The claim that no refund clause is available is accepted in part (see below).

The rider's claims. The POL-NS-21 and POL-GEN-02 claims that arrival is uncorroborated and the trace silent over the waiting window are accepted. The POL-GEN-26 escalation claim is accepted, and is the ruling here. The POL-NS-24 claim is accepted only to the effect that the deadline cannot be fixed: an on-demand trip has no scheduled_at, driver_deadline.deadline is null, and POL-NS-24's note routes that to POL-GEN-26 rather than to a FULL_REFUND, so no refund issues from it. The POL-NS-23 concession that contact was met is accepted. The POL-GEN-03 claim that the rider is out of pocket 5.00 SGD is accepted as fact (EV-FARE-06061: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), but on escalation the amount is held, so no refund is ordered now.

Referrals and amounts. The fee charged is exactly the policy fee of 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire; the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit does not fire because contact was attempted; and the POL-NS-25 repeat no-show referral does not fire because the field is absent and the fee does not stand. No referral is added, and no monetary outcome issues.

Open question for the reviewer: whether the driver was at Block 14, Eunos Crescent during the 13:11:50-13:16:50 free-wait window and cancelled only after it. The impaired GPS trace (EV-GPS-06061, weight 0.6) cannot establish it, and the arrival tap, push notification and wait timer rest on the same button press.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case turns on one fact — whether the driver was actually at Block 14, Eunos Crescent, and when — because the 5.00 SGD no-show fee depends on a 5-minute free wait that can only start once he is there. On this record that fact cannot be established, so the case goes to a human reviewer and the 5.00 SGD is held: it is neither refunded to the rider nor paid out to the driver for now.

WHY THE ARRIVAL IS UNDECIDED. The category's arrival test treats the driver as at the pickup only when the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace inside 50 m and a 120 s window. EV-GPS-06061 reports corroborated = false and nearest_fix = null. That trace is impaired: weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION — a single 640 s gap from 13:08:50 to 13:19:30 that swallows the 13:11:50 arrival marker, the whole free-wait window (13:11:50–13:16:50) and the 13:18:20 cancellation, with coverage at 28.6% (8 fixes against a 30 s interval). POL-NS-08(b) makes a gap longer than 120 s inside the waiting window a policy-level impairment, and the test here has no fix inside the window it reads at all.

THE DRIVER'S CASE (POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22, POL-GEN-02). You are right that on an on-demand trip the free wait runs from arrival, and that 390 s from the arrival marker to the cancellation is 90 s past the end of it. But the marker you measure from is the driver's own "arrived" tap, and a status a party sets records only that the party set it; the 13:11:54 "driver has arrived" push and the 13:11:55 wait timer are platform records of that same tap and do not independently establish presence. The chat messages ("Reached Blk 14 drop off" 13:12:10, "Waiting" 13:15:00) and the counterparty statement ("I was there") are accounts offered in place of a GPS reading the test admits none of, so they do not stand in for it. The arrival is therefore not made out, and DRIVER_COMPENSATION at 5.00 SGD under POL-NS-22 cannot issue. I have disclosed EV-GPS-06061, its weight and its issue code as POL-GEN-02(1) requires.

THE RIDER'S CASE (POL-NS-21, POL-GEN-26, POL-NS-24, POL-GEN-03). The same impairment cuts the other way. An undecided limb supports neither a payment that needs the clause to hold nor a refund that needs it to fail, so the fee is not voided either and FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD is not available. Your money point is accurate on the figures — EV-FARE-06061 shows cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, with refund_if_voided_sgd 5.00 — but the money is not the issue; the arrival is. On POL-NS-24, the driver no-show clause, this trip is on-demand with scheduled_at null, so there is no scheduled time to miss and no deadline to fix; as that clause's own note says, where the record carries none and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies — which is where we land, by escalation rather than by a refund.

WHAT DECIDES IT. POL-GEN-26: where a fact a rule of this version needs — here, when the driver arrived, and so whether the free wait ever began — cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is impaired, the case is escalated and the open question is stated. The open question for the reviewer is when, and whether, the driver was at Block 14 between roughly 13:09 and 13:19:30, the stretch the trace leaves unobserved.

CONTACT OBLIGATION (POL-NS-23) — NOT A GROUND FOR REFUND. EV-CHAT-06061 (complete, weight 1.0) shows two driver messages at 13:12:10 and 13:15:00, and EV-TRIP-06061 shows one in-app call placed at 13:14:20, all before the 13:18:20 cancellation; the clause requires a call to be placed, not answered, so the 20 s unanswered ring meets it. Both sides accept this limb is met, and it voids nothing.

NO REFERRAL FIRES. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not apply; rider_profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d count at or above 3, so POL-NS-25 does not apply; and POL-NS-24's goodwill credit needs the driver to have both failed to arrive and failed to attempt contact, and contact was in fact attempted. The 5.00 SGD is held rather than collected or refunded.

CONFIDENCE. 0.6, capped by EV-GPS-06061 (weight 0.6) — the impaired artifact the escalation rests on. POL-NS-26 and POL-GEN-22 require no higher bar for a no-show below 10.00 SGD with no fraud or safety flag.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute is about the 5.00 SGD no-show fee on trip TRP-06061 (EV-FARE-06061: cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, payment_status CHARGED). The rider says the driver never came to Block 14; the driver says he was there. The whole case turns on one fact: whether the driver was physically at the pickup, because on this on-demand trip (scheduled_at null) the 300 s free wait that POL-NS-21 requires runs from the driver's arrival.

Under this category's arrival test, the driver is at the pickup only when the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace inside a 50 m radius (STANDARD). That trace, EV-GPS-06061, is IMPAIRED: issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight_multiplier 0.6. It carries a single 640 s gap from 13:08:50 to 13:19:30 that swallows the 13:11:50 arrival marker, the entire free-wait window and the 13:18:20 cancellation; its own derived arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null, and there is no fix at all inside the window. The 13:11:50 'driver arrived' entry is an arrival tap — a status the driver set — and the driver's chat messages ('Reached Blk 14 drop off', 13:12:10; 'Waiting', 13:15:00) and his counterparty statement ('I was there') only re-assert what the impaired trace cannot check: they stand in for the test exactly where it admitted no reading, so they neither carry the arrival nor lift the 0.6 cap.

That leaves the arrival — and with it the free-wait start the fee depends on — undecided, and an undecided limb supports neither the payment the driver claims nor the refund the rider seeks. POL-GEN-26 is directly on point: where a fact a rule needs (here, when the driver arrived) cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is impaired, the case is escalated and the open question stated. The 5.00 SGD is therefore held, neither collected nor refunded.

On the points both sides agree: the contact obligation is met. EV-CHAT-06061 (COMPLETE) shows the driver's two in-app messages and EV-TRIP-06061 shows his in-app call at 13:14:20, all before the 13:18:20 cancellation, so POL-NS-23 does not void the fee and no FULL_REFUND arises on that limb. POL-NS-24 gives no refund either — this on-demand trip has no scheduled pickup time, so none was missed. The driver's POL-NS-22 claim for DRIVER_COMPENSATION fails because the free-wait precondition it needs is precisely the limb left undecided (the 390 s is measured from the uncorroborated arrival tap, not from an established arrival). No POL-NS-24 goodwill credit arises, since contact was attempted, and the fee charged equals the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral fires. Confidence is capped at 0.6, the weight of the impaired GPS artifact that carries the deciding fact (POL-GEN-02(2)).

Open question for the human reviewer: establish whether the driver was physically at Block 14, Eunos Crescent at about 13:11:50 on 2026-10-04 — e.g. from vehicle telemetry or another independent record — and so whether the 300 s free wait validly ran before the 13:18:20 no-show cancellation. Until that is resolved the 5.00 SGD stays held.

ledger.claim: The arrival that starts the free wait is not established on this record. Under the category's arrival test the driver is at the pickup only when the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m and the 120 s window, and the trace's own derived arrival check returns corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null. The 13:11:50 'driver arrived' event therefore rests on the driver's button press alone, and the driver's counterparty statement ('I was there') has nothing behind it but that button. EV-GPS-06061 is impaired - issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight_multiplier 0.6 - its only gap being 640 s, from 13:08:50 to 13:19:30, which straddles the arrival marker, the free-wait window and the cancellation, with the fixes either side several hundred metres from the pickup.

The trace is silent on the one interval the fee depends on. The free wait for this on-demand trip runs 13:11:50 to 13:16:50 under POL-NS-21, and EV-GPS-06061 carries no fix inside it at all: the single 640 s gap swallows the entire waiting window, coverage_pct is 28.6 and there are 8 fixes against a 30 s expected interval. That artifact is impaired - GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight 0.6 - so the interval the driver's presence turns on is precisely the interval with no location evidence, and POL-GEN-02 caps any confidence in it at 0.6.

The record's 390 s is measured from an arrival event that the GPS trace does not corroborate, so the fee's precondition is not made out on this evidence: a 5.00 SGD charge cannot stand on a timer whose start has no support beyond the app's own button press.

ledger.claim: The fact this case turns on - whether the driver was at Block 14, and when - cannot be established, because the only artifact that could corroborate it is impaired across exactly the relevant interval. POL-GEN-26 provides that where a fact a rule of this version needs cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired, the case is escalated and the open question stated, and no outcome is inferred from the absence except where a rule says so. EV-GPS-06061 is impaired (GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight 0.6). ESCALATE is the rider-favourable reading here: the 5.00 SGD is held rather than collected, while NO_ACTION would leave the rider carrying it.

POL-NS-24 refunds in full any fee charged where the driver fails to arrive at the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes. This trip was on-demand with no scheduled_at, so the deadline cannot be fixed from the record (driver_deadline.deadline is null) - and the arrival that would fix it is uncorroborated. On the clause's own reading, where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies. Either way the charge is not left standing on this record: the driver either did not arrive (full refund) or arrival cannot be established (escalation, fee held). EV-GPS-06061 is impaired, issue GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, weight 0.6.

The money is still with the platform and still on the rider. EV-FARE-06061 shows payment_status CHARGED, cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the rider is out of pocket the whole contested amount. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is read party-relative against the rider who filed: the rider is owed the disputed charge back, so any ruling that voids the fee is FULL_REFUND of the whole 5.00 SGD (the ledger's refund_if_voided_sgd is 5.00), and NO_ACTION would simply preserve the present state in which the rider pays.

The rider does not put its case on POL-NS-23, and says so plainly rather than stretching the point: EV-CHAT-06061 shows two in-app messages (13:12:10 and 13:15:00) and EV-TRIP-06061 shows one in-app call placed at 13:14:20, all before the 13:18:20 cancellation, and the derived obligation_met is true. The contact limb is met on the face of the record. The rider's case is the arrival limb, not this one.

This is an on-demand trip — scheduled_at is null — so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival, not from any schedule. The trip record shows the driver marking arrived at 13:11:50, the free-wait timer starting at 13:11:55 and expiring at 13:16:55, and the cancellation at 13:18:20: 390 s after arrival, 90 s past the end of the free wait. On those timings the driver cancelled only after the wait had fully run, which is exactly what POL-NS-21 permits.

POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the driver failed to message AND call before cancelling. Both limbs are satisfied on the COMPLETE records: the chat log carries two in-app messages sent by the driver, at 13:12:10 and 13:15:00, and the trip record carries an in-app call placed by the driver at 13:14:20 — all three before the 13:18:20 cancellation. The clause requires a call to be placed, not answered, so the 20 s unanswered ring-out satisfies it. The contact obligation is met and there is no ground to void the fee.

The payments ledger shows exactly 5.00 SGD charged for the cancellation — the policy fee — with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has yet moved. Under POL-NS-22, where the free wait has run and the fee stands, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged, 5.00 SGD; POL-GEN-03 confirms that figure is the money the ruling moves, not a second payment.

No FULL_REFUND is available to the rider on this record. On a no-show charge only POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-24 favour the rider, and both fail: the contact obligation was met (POL-NS-23), and POL-NS-24 needs a scheduled pickup time the driver missed by five minutes, but this trip is on-demand with scheduled_at null, so there is no scheduled time to miss and no deadline to fix. The rider's 'he never came' account therefore has no refund clause to stand on, and the present charge must be left intact.

I disclose rather than hide the state of the trace: the GPS artifact is IMPAIRED, weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, and its derived arrival check reports corroborated false with nearest_fix null. It cannot be presented as clean corroboration. But a 640 s gap is absent data, not evidence that the driver was somewhere else, and the arrival event, the 'driver has arrived' push notification to the rider at 13:11:54 and the free-wait timer are all carried independently on the COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0. The impairment caps the weight of the trace; it does not erase the platform record of arrival.

Even on the most sceptical reading of the impaired trace — that the arrival is not GPS-corroborated — the result is not a refund. POL-GEN-26 sends a case to human review precisely where a needed fact (here, when the driver arrived) cannot be established on impaired evidence, and on escalation the amount is held, not returned. That is the floor of this case, and it still leaves the 5.00 SGD with the driver rather than the rider.
